acceptance: A change that alters a pure-Python generator's SF 1 output size by more than the baseline tolerance fails a required check unless the baseline is updated in the same change (shown with a test or a probe PR).
The check is wired into required CI.
context: Filed 2026-11-12 from the scale-factor follow-up and TPC-DI generator work of 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12: identified during that work and not addressed.
description:
## Problem
BenchBox-dev/benchbox#4149 raised TPC-DI SF 1 fact rows from 275,000 to 6.77 million. PR CI and the local and hosted reviews were green. Two things then went wrong after merge:
- `tests/unit/generators/sf1_size_baseline.json` still said 160,094,804 bytes for `tpcdi` while the generator produced about three times that. No test compares the baseline with generated data in the fast tier (`test_measure_one_runs_a_lightweight_generator_end_to_end` is marked slow and measures another benchmark), so the site published two different TPC-DI sizes until #4171 corrected the baseline by hand.
- Trunk UAT 43154678095 timed out on Spark and DataFusion TPC-DI at SF 1 (see `tpcdi-sf1-slowdown-after-linear-fact-scaling`), because nothing before merge ran the benchmark at the new volume.

## Change
Add a pre-merge signal for data-volume changes. Options: a path-filtered CI job that re-measures the SF 1 size for a benchmark whose generator or `generator_specs.yaml` changed and fails outside the baseline tolerance; a preflight guard that requires a baseline update when a generator spec file changes; a required DuckDB smoke run at SF 1 for the touched benchmark.

## Guardrails
- Keep it path-filtered: measuring every benchmark at SF 1 is heavy.
- The baseline feeds the site through `scripts/doc_contracts.py`, so a baseline change must reach the site page in step.
